Introduction¶

Note

This is just the intro of Guild Wars taken directly from the game. This is used to quickly introduce what is guild war to new players before reading the rest of this guide.

Guild War Overview¶

Guild War has two modes: League and Ranked Matches.

League:

Held Saturdays and Sundays at 20:30. Each season consists of three phases.

Prep Phase (1 week):

All guilds are regrouped.

Placement Matches (2 weeks):

Held every Saturdays and Sundays at 20:30. Guilds are assigned to Jesting Sage, Jesting Cod, Jesting Hero, or Stealth Jester groups based on results.

Regular Season Phase (10 weeks, 2 weeks per round):

Intra-group matches. Top 4 promote, bottom 4 demote each round. At season end, all Guilds in Jesting Sage, Jesting Cod and Jesting Hero groups, plus top-ranked Guilds in Stealth Jester group, automatically qualify for the next League. Others must qualify via Matchmaking.

Ranked Matches:

Available to Guild Management and Commanders on Saturdays and Sundays from 20:30 to 23:00. League participants can only join Ranked Matches after their League match ends.

Note

Max 30 players per Guild per match. Players can only represent one Guild per day.

Winning Conditions¶

  1. Move the opponent’s Fortune Tree to your camp to win instantly.

  2. If neither side succeeds, the Guild that moved the tree further wins.

  3. If the tree wasn’t moved, the winner is decided by (in order of priority):

    1. remaining Goose HP

    2. number of remaining Bulwarks

    3. remaining Bulwark HP.

Bulwark¶

  • Bulwark consists of up to 3 players. Commanders assign initial defenders. Players can join or leave freely during combat. If there are still available spots, nearby players may join Bulwark.

  • Surviving Bulwarks generate Fun Coins every 30 seconds.

  • Nearby allies grant additional damage reduction to the Bulwark.

Command¶

  • The Guild Leader and Deputy Leaders are Commanders by default. The Leader may also appoint other members as Commanders. Commanders can purchase Commander Buffs and Battlefield Items, assign Bulwark defenders, etc.

  • Surviving Bulwarks periodically generate Fun Coins. Killing monsters and Bosses yields massive Fun Coins.

Giant Guardian Goose¶

  • Players must break through the Giant Guardian Goose’s defense before moving the Fortune Tree.

  • Learn Guild Techniques or use Commander Buffs to deal massive damage to the Giant Guardian Goose.

Fortune Tree¶

  • The Fortune Tree can be moved only after defeating the Giant Guardian Goose.

  • Move the opponent’s Fortune Tree to your camp to win instantly.

  • Players can only move the enemy Fortune Tree. If the player’s team Fortune Tree is moved, they cannot move it back.

  • Moving the Fortune Tree is slower if enemies are nearby. With 5 enemies nearby, the Fortune Tree stops moving.

Special Mechanics¶

  1. Healing reduced by 30%. Potion recovery reduced by 60%.

  2. Healing from common Martial Skills only applies to your team, while exclusive Guild War skills can apply to the whole Guild.

  3. All Stagger effects are reduced in Guild War to improve team fights.

  4. The spawn point is a Safe Zone. Players in the Safe Zone cannot take damage from or deal damage to enemies.

  5. You will be automatically removed from Guild War after 3 minutes of inactivity.
